title: Renck: Broncos' Sean Payton makes Seahawks seasick, Bo Nix competent long enough for Wil Lutz to save day
text:
Yes, the Broncos are back. Sort of. Thanks to Ja’Quan McMillian’s interception on Seattle’s first possession in the extra period. It set up Wil Lutz’s 53-yard walkoff..
Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on during the first half of a game against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver.
Unbelievably, after six games, Sean Payton has the Broncos in position to reach their goals in the most obvious, if not nauseating and dizzying, of ways after an overtime victory. With him calling plays, his quarterback looked briefly competent, and Vance Joseph threw so many blitzes and punches in so many directions that he just had to make sure he didn’t hit the ring posts or goal posts. The Broncos are back.
Barely, if you watched the second half, and especially the 15-second drive with 1:25 remaining. Yes, they are back. Sort of. Thanks to Ja’Quan McMillian’s interception on Seattle’s first extra-period possession.
It set up Wil Lutz’s 53-yard walkoff. You can say the Broncos never left, but they were dissolving as a contender, with an offense that started games like their cleats were on their wrong feet and with a quarterback whose feet looked like they were on the wrong ankles. The Broncos can repeat as AFC champs. Not playing like they did the final 35 minutes.
But they can without turnovers, given the nastiness of the defense. Following a long weekend, they face the Arizona Cardinals — as long as Nathaniel Hackett is calling plays, it is impossible to see Denver losing — before a home rematch with the Chiefs on Nov. 1. This lingers as a must-win if the Broncos want to get those division title caps that Payton deposits into the nearest trash bin. This is what comes with Payton — lavish expectations.
Even if his third-down pass after Kris Abrams-Draine’s fourth-quarter interception ranked confusing at best and foolish at worst. Payton took the Denver job to win another Super Bowl and cement a Hall of Fame legacy. Somewhat impossibly, given the scoring problems through three quarters the past two seasons, he can live up to his own hype. The offense, in the name of transparency, was not good in prime time.
Entering the fourth quarter, they had 11 first downs on the two touchdown drives and one on all others. Remember, the Broncos entered the game ranked 31st in first-half offense. They were tied with Tennessee, whose quarterback looks like he is a fish on a bicycle, alternating misfires with interceptions.
Running back RJ Harvey of the Denver Broncos runs through a tackle by defensive end Mike Morris of the Seattle Seahawks during the first half of a game on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver. Nix was the reason for pessimism. Broncos Country wasn’t jumping off the bandwagon, but fans were familiarizing themselves with the nearest exits.
Payton relieving Davis Webb of his play-calling duties did not pay dividends against the Chargers. But it made a difference against the Seahawks in the first half. Payton talks about quarterbacks in analogies. He says it is important to remove them from the high dive — since all those not named Drew Brees are not executing Triple Lindy dives.
Against the Seahawks early, Payton played all of Nix’s favorite hits. There were well-timed screens against pressure. A few targets in the middle of the field. And yes, the artist formerly known as Courtland Sutton appeared on drag routes on third down.
Nix went 10 for 15 for 78 yards in the first half. No touchdowns. But no interceptions or sacks, either. His 2.54 seconds from snap to release was the quickest of his career.
It became obvious Payton identified — as he is wont to do — a path to victory as Denver posted a 14-3 halftime lead. Turtling, anyone? It is possible, if not painful, to tuck the head into a shell when the defense is a menace. There was a point early in the fourth where Payton crouched with his hands on his knees.
His back aches from disc pain. If anyone should have been gulping Doan’s extra-strength caplets, it was Joseph. Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold admitted early in his career that he saw ghosts. He can be excused for seeing Malcolm McDowell in “A Clockwork Orange.
” The Broncos lived in Darnold’s grill; no one more than Allen, whose J.J. Watt Lite impersonation is becoming more spot on with each passing week. The Seahawks are champs in name only. This is not the team that clobbered the Patriots because their offense is one-dimensional without running back Kenneth Walker and highly-touted rookie Jadarian Price injured.
Seattle’s playbook was to throw to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and hope that Darnold remained upright for half of those attempts. It wasn’t an inspiring triumph. But it was fun for those who grew up with the Orange Crush of 1977 and the Orange Rush of 2015. The Broncos had yielded six first downs through three quarters.
Because these are the Broncos, it came with accompanying drama. Denver’s listless offense left Denver weary, vulnerable, as Seattle’s reserve running backs gained traction. Darnold found gold in the back of the end zone on a tipped pass by cornerback Jahdae Barron that somehow Rashid Shaheed snared while staying in bounds. Leading 14-11, the full-throated crowd growing restless, Nix reverted back to his slump.
He held the ball too long on first down, running out of bounds. And on third down, he curled into a ball, sacked for a loss that forced Denver to lean on Crawshaw and the hands-on-hips defense.
